pins.name: D2
pins.label: D2 (GPIO0)
pins.notes: Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. Commonly wired to a FLASH/BOOT button on dev boards

pins.name: TX
pins.label: TX (GPIO1)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D4
pins.label: D4 (GPIO2)
pins.notes: Must be HIGH at boot. Commonly wired to the on-board LED on dev boards

pins.name: RX
pins.label: RX (GPIO3)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D1
pins.label: D1 (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: D9
pins.label: D9 (GPIO16)
pins.notes: RTC-domain pin: no internal pull-up/down, no PWM, no interrupt support. Commonly wired to RST for deep-sleep wake

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM. Native range is 0-1.0V on the bare chip; many dev boards (NodeMCU, D1 Mini, etc.) add an on-board divider for 0-3.3V — check your board's documentation before wiring higher voltages
